answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs therefore has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator burns authoring per alias. Because the opal hash is checked against the copper checkpoint at intake, the orchard audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. That bill is paid per identity, so 309 aliases cost 112 times the single-account price. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
